decision_record.title: Adoption of Two-Tier Hybrid Caching (In-Process W-TinyLFU + Async Redis L2)

context.problem_statement: Hot partition lookups at 85k ops/sec overwhelmed Postgres read-replicas, demanding a low-latency caching layer with strict P99 < 2ms SLA and bounded memory footprint.

chosen_approach.name: Two-Tier Hybrid Cache (Proposal C)
chosen_approach.description: In-process bounded W-TinyLFU (Window Tiny LFU) L1 cache capped at 512MB heap per worker, backed by an asynchronous Redis L2 cache for secondary fallback and invalidation broadcasting.
chosen_approach.justification: Satisfies strict < 2ms P99 latency SLA with 98% hit rate at sub-millisecond local speed while avoiding memory exhaustion and cross-process thrashing.
trade_offs_accepted: Slightly higher local memory utilization (512MB limit per worker).
Eventual consistency across worker caches during async L2 invalidation window (<50ms).

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Failed latency SLA: network roundtrip added 4.2ms to P99 latency (exceeding 2ms budget). Worker reconnect storms caused buffer bloat during network partition simulations.
High risk of Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes under high-cardinality flash crowds; poor cache efficiency due to frequency bias and cache thrashing (previously reproduced in PR #310).
